note: Reel 14: The Jam With No Cause. A Bengaluru jam with nothing at its front; Sugiyama et al. 2008 (22 cars, a 230 m circle, one rule: drive steadily) made one from nothing; a small slowdown amplifies car by car until someone stops; the jam travels backwards at about bicycle speed (15 +/- 5 km/h on highways); the root cause is our late reactions; Stern et al. 2018: one controlled car on a 260 m ring dampened the waves (up to 40% less fuel); leave a gap: you could end a jam, or start it (the loop). Kokoro af_heart, speed 1.0. Numbers as words. 'Bengaluru' (Kannada [beŋɡəɭuːɾu]): misaki's plain spelling reads /bˈɛŋɡələɹˌu/, 'BENG-guh-luh-roo', the long 'loo' lost; the phoneme ear heard the third syllable as ɚ/ᵻ/ɪ in s01, s01b, s01c. Round 2 (s01d–g): the length mark works (the third syllable heard as uː); misaki turns ɾ into its flap T, which English-only ears hear as d ('Bangaludu', small.en) but large-v3 heard as Bengaluru: the American flap is the Kannada tap; the Indian e came out as 'bay'/'bing', the American ɛ as a clean 'beng'. Round 3 (s01h–k): /bˌɛŋɡəlˈuːTu/ (s01i) was heard as b ɛ ŋ ɡ ə l uː (tap) u, 'beng-ga-LOO-ru', the Kannada [beŋɡəɭuːɾu] but for the retroflex l, by both Whispers as Bengaluru, phoneme error 10 %: s01 uses it. s12 and s13 read at 0.88 (they came out at 4.0–4.7 words a second).

lines.text: This Bengaluru traffic jam has no cause.
lines.text_kokoro: This [Bengaluru](/bˌɛŋɡəlˈuːTu/) traffic jam has no cause.

lines.text: Follow it to the front: no accident, no signal, not even a pothole.
In two thousand eight, scientists in Japan made a jam out of nothing.
Twenty-two cars, one circle, one rule: keep a steady speed.
Then one driver slowed down. Just a little.
The one behind reacted a beat late and braked harder. The next, harder still, until someone stopped.
And the jam moved backwards, about as fast as a bicycle.
The driver who started it never knew.
That's the root cause: not the road. It's us, braking a beat too late.
In two thousand eighteen, one self-driving car on a ring like this held a steady speed.
So leave a gap. You could be the one who ends a jam.
Or the one who starts it.
